# Decisions: Nexus Code v1.0.0

This file records only consequential decisions that were unresolved when the audit finished. On 2026-10-14 the owner authorized applying the recommended option for every outstanding decision. ("You are authorized to apply your recommendations for the best decisions for the project on any outstanding decisions in the plans/specs.") Each entry is therefore marked **RESOLVED (delegated)**. The options, tradeoffs and affected requirements are kept so the owner can reverse any decision later. A reversal would change the linked specs, plans and gates.

Some decisions cannot be carried out by an implementer alone. They need an external action, and those actions are listed in the last section. The audit did not perform any of them.

| ID | Decision | Resolution | Blocks execution? |
|---|---|---|---|
| [DEC-01](#dec-01-default-execution-posture) | Default execution posture | Review by default; auto only in trusted workspaces | No (resolved) |
| [DEC-02](#dec-02-role-of-the-repl) | Role of the REPL | Supported secondary surface; TUI primary; top-level flags implemented | No |
| [DEC-03](#dec-03-team-and-operation-scope-in-v1) | `/team` and `nexus operation` in v1 | Shipped as **experimental**; data-loss fix still a blocker | No |
| [DEC-04](#dec-04-issue-12-open-normative-blockers) | Issue #12 open blockers | EXT-004 implemented; CTX-001 partially implemented; CTX-002 descoped post-v1 | No |
| [DEC-05](#dec-05-v1-evaluation-protocol-and-thresholds) | Evaluation protocol and thresholds | 40 held-out T2 tasks, 5 runs, 2 peers, thresholds below | Needs an external author (see actions) |
| [DEC-06](#dec-06-supported-providers-for-v1) | Supported providers | Local OpenAI-compatible + OpenRouter supported; others experimental until live-verified | No |
| [DEC-07](#dec-07-experimental-surfaces-nexus-eval-tdd-team-roles) | `nexus eval`, `/tdd`, team roles | eval and tdd experimental; eval's workspace mutation fixed; role tool sets enforced | No |
| [DEC-08](#dec-08-version-identity-and-stale-v1x-tags) | Version identity, stale v1.x tags | `package.json` is the source of truth; local v1.x tags deleted (owner action) | No |
| [DEC-09](#dec-09-release-provenance-mechanism) | Release provenance | GitHub artifact attestations | No |
| [DEC-10](#dec-10-tracking-of-clidist) | Tracking of `cli/dist` | Untrack | No |
| [DEC-11](#dec-11-retention-defaults) | Retention defaults | 90 days / 2 GB; audit log 10 MB × 5; first GC needs acknowledgement | No |
| [DEC-12](#dec-12-platform-scope) | Platform scope | Linux x86-64 glibc only for v1.0.0 | No |
| [DEC-13](#dec-13-contest-track-disposition) | Contest track | Separate track; docs and CI fix immediately; submission states operator-host only | Owner confirms deadline status |
| [DEC-14](#dec-14-free-text-on-the-command-line) | Free text on the command line | Explicit `nexus run` required | No |
| [DEC-15](#dec-15-knowledge-auto-extraction) | Knowledge auto-extraction | Off by default, opt-in | No |

---

## DEC-01: Default execution posture

**Question.** What protects the user by default from model-initiated command execution and network egress? See SEC-01, VER-01, HIST-05 and TUI-07.

| Option | Description | Tradeoffs |
|---|---|---|
| A | Review by default: write, exec and egress ask | Safest. More prompts. Changes existing users' habits. |
| B | Auto with an enforced sandbox by default | Few prompts. bwrap is unavailable on some hosts (WSL, rootless containers), and the Docker fallback is unpinned and networked. Egress is unsolved. |
| **C (chosen)** | Posture follows workspace trust. **Untrusted workspace → review** for `write_workspace`, `exec`, `egress` and `context_inject`. **Trusted workspace → auto** for `write_workspace` and `exec`; `egress` asks once per origin per session. `--yes` or `NEXUS_APPROVAL_MODE=auto` force auto. `--sandbox` stays available. | Safe for cloned or unknown repos. Low friction on the operator's own repos after one `nexus trust .`. Reuses the existing trust store, so there is no new concept. |
| D | Keep auto | Contradicts REQ-SEC-101; rejected. |

**Rationale.** The threat that matters is content from an untrusted repository or the web. Trust is the existing per-workspace boundary that MCP and plugins already honour. Option C closes SEC-01 and VER-01 on exactly the inputs that cause them, and keeps the daily-driver experience on trusted repos.

**Further rules:**
- Headless `nexus run` with no TTY: decision-required calls are DENIED with a typed reason unless `--yes` is given.
- The eval and demo runners pass `--yes` explicitly.

**Affected requirements:** REQ-SEC-101, 102 and 119; REQ-TUI-102; SPEC-01; PLAN-01; ACC-SAFE-01.

## DEC-02: Role of the REPL

**Options.** (A) Remove the REPL. **(B, chosen)** The REPL is a supported secondary surface: used for non-TTY input, scripting and fallback, with its approvals fixed to the TUI's standard. (C) The REPL stays the default.

**Rationale.** The REPL is the only interactive surface when stdin or stdout is not a terminal, and when the Rust TUI is missing. Removing it loses a fallback. Keeping it as the default contradicts UI-004.

**Also decided.** The top-level flags `--approve`, `-r/--resume [id]`, `--repl` and `--live` are **implemented** rather than removed from the docs, because USER_MANUAL already teaches them.

**Affected requirements:** REQ-REL-101, REQ-REL-102, REQ-SEC-103.

## DEC-03: Team and operation scope in v1

**Options.** (A) Fully supported. **(B, chosen)** Shipped and labelled **experimental** in help and docs. Excluded from the qualification task-quality claims. But the following are still fixed for v1:
- **AGT-02a** (compaction originals lost on resume): BLOCKER, because it silently loses durable state behind a documented guarantee.
- **AGT-02b–d and AGT-11**: RELEASE-REQUIRED.

(C) Remove the commands.

**Rationale.** Evidence for multi-unit convergence is thin. EXECUTION_CONVERGENCE lists I3, I4 and a stale-lock race as open, and post-remediation dogfooding was INTEGRATION_BLOCKED. Removing the commands throws away working code. Silent data loss is not acceptable even in experimental features.

**Affected requirements:** REQ-AGT-102, 103, 107; SPEC-04.

## DEC-04: Issue #12 open normative blockers

| Item | Resolution | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EXT-004 (middleware before/after audit) | **Implement** (SPEC-03 §3.5) | Small change. Plugins can rewrite tool I/O silently today. |
| CTX-001 (per-item provenance for injected context) | **Partially implement**: skills, knowledge and other injected context carry source path and trust state (SPEC-03 §3.4). The full provenance graph is post-v1. | The risky injected sources are covered. A full implementation is a large redesign with low marginal safety benefit once trust gating exists. |
| CTX-002 (freshness and version applicability of knowledge) | **Descoped to post-v1**, with this written rationale: auto-extraction is off by default (DEC-15) and knowledge is trust-gated, so stale knowledge can only come from the operator's own explicit saves. | Accepted risk, recorded. |
| UI-006/007, DEDUP-003, "no Git remote", SUBP-004/005 deferrals | **Recorded as superseded** in REQUIREMENTS §2 (Ratatui adopted; on-demand tool groups; public GitHub). SUBP-004 and SUBP-005 are replaced by SPEC-02. | Governance hygiene (HIST-11). |

## DEC-05: v1 evaluation protocol and thresholds

**Chosen protocol (SPEC-10):**
- 40 held-out T2 tasks, at least 20 from external repositories at pinned commits, across JS/TS, Python, Rust and Go, with at least 6 per class (bugfix, feature, refactor, debug).
- 5 runs per task and configuration.
- Peers: Goose and OpenCode, on the same model and budgets.
- 8 T4 fault classes × 5 runs.
- 8 T3 long tasks × 5 runs.

**Thresholds, all must hold:**

| Metric | Threshold |
|---|---|
| False VERIFIED | **0** (hard) |
| Held-out T2 pooled hidden-test correctness | **≥ 60% absolute** and **≥ (best matched peer − 10 points)** |
| Correctness per task class | ≥ 40% |
| Crash rate | ≤ 2% |
| Regression rate | ≤ 5% |
| T4 outcome truthfulness | 100% |
| T4 hangs beyond budget + 5 min | 0 |
| T3 false-absence | 0 |
| T3 steering honoured | ≥ 95% |
| `run`-mode operator interventions | 0 |

**Task authorship.** The held-out half must be authored without access to Nexus's development set and tuning history. The first preference is a person other than the implementer. If none is available, use a separately-run agent session given only this task schema and the external repositories, with no Nexus source access. Its sha256 manifest is committed before the RC freeze. That fallback is weaker independence and must be stated in the qualification report.

**Rationale.** These figures are the pilot's pre-registered thresholds (eval/README), tightened where the pilot showed weakness: false VERIFIED, crash accounting. The absolute floor prevents "beat a weak peer" from passing. Thresholds are fixed **before** the RC run.

## DEC-06: Supported providers for v1

| Tier | Providers | Condition |
|---|---|---|
| **Supported** | OpenAI-compatible local servers (llama.cpp server, vLLM, LM Studio, Ollama) | The release notes name the server kinds that pass the standalone matrix (≥ 2 required). Others are listed as "compatible, not qualified". |
| **Supported (optional integration)** | homelab-ai gateway | Never required (standalone gate). |
| **Supported** | OpenRouter | Already live-verified historically; re-verify at RC. |
| **Experimental → Supported if live-verified at RC** | OpenAI (Responses), Anthropic (Messages), generic compatible cloud | `nexus providers verify` live PASS archived at RC; otherwise they stay experimental. |
| **Experimental (always)** | ChatGPT sign-in, Copilot sign-in | They use unofficial OAuth flows with terms-of-service and stability risk. Opt-in with a visible warning. |

## DEC-07: Experimental surfaces (`nexus eval`, `/tdd`, team roles)

- **`nexus eval`.** Labelled experimental. Its scoring is not fixed in v1, but its unsafe `git checkout` in the operator's workspace **is** fixed: it must run in a worktree (VER-07a). It is excluded from all claims. The SPEC-10 harness (`eval/`) is the qualification tool.
- **`/tdd` / `--tdd`.** Labelled experimental. Fixing the phase enforcement is post-v1.
- **Team roles.** Reviewer and researcher units run with a **read-only tool set** (cheap and safety-relevant). Other role allowlists are post-v1.

## DEC-08: Version identity and stale v1.x tags

- `package.json` is the single source of truth. `scripts/sync-version.mjs` updates `cli/package.json` and `core/Cargo.toml`. Release CI asserts that all three equal the tag.
- Release line: `v1.0.0-rc.N` prereleases, then `v1.0.0`.
- The local-only tags `v1.1.0`, `v1.2.0` and `v1.2.1` are to be **deleted locally**: `git tag -d v1.1.0 v1.2.0 v1.2.1`. They are not on origin and are not ancestors of main. They sort above v1.0.0 and would confuse `git describe` and the tooling. This is an owner action (see the last section) because it removes local references.

## DEC-09: Release provenance mechanism

**Chosen:** GitHub artifact attestations (`actions/attest-build-provenance`). Users verify with `gh attestation verify`. SHA256SUMS is kept. There is no separate GPG or minisign key to manage.

**Tradeoff:** verification needs the `gh` CLI or the Sigstore tooling. The installer verifies only when `gh` is present, and checksums are always verified.

## DEC-10: Tracking of `cli/dist`

**Chosen:** stop tracking `cli/dist`. Remove it from git, add it to `.gitignore`, and build it in CI and packaging. Checkout users already need `make build` for the Rust binaries.

**Tradeoff:** a fresh clone needs one build step for the TS side too; the docs already state `make build`.

## DEC-11: Retention defaults

**Chosen:**
- Keep tasks, sessions, checkpoints and flights for 90 days or up to 2 GB in total, whichever limit is hit first. Never remove the current session or pinned sessions.
- Rotate `audit.log` at 10 MB, keeping 5 files.
- Automatic GC runs at most daily. The first run after upgrade needs acknowledgement, or `NEXUS_GC=auto`.

## DEC-12: Platform scope

**Chosen:** Linux x86-64, glibc ≥ 2.35, Node ≥ 20 for v1.0.0, which is what is built and tested. The docs keep the conservative "≥ 2.35" claim; the binaries reference glibc symbols ≤ 2.34. macOS, arm64 and musl are post-v1 roadmap items.

## DEC-13: Contest track disposition

**Chosen:**
- The contest is a separate track (SPEC-C1) and never gates the client.
- The CON-001 documentation and CI correction is made immediately, because it currently misdirects judges to an unauthenticated legacy Worker.
- Until CON-102–106 are delivered and a clean-account run exists, all contest material states "reproduced on the operator host only".

**Owner check needed:** whether the contest deadline (2026-10-14) still admits repository changes. If it does not, the corrections land after the contest, marked post-submission.

## DEC-14: Free text on the command line

**Chosen:** an unknown first word is an error. Free text runs only through `nexus run "<text>"` or the interactive prompt. This removes REL-03's accidental agent launches.

## DEC-15: Knowledge auto-extraction

**Chosen:** off by default; opt-in with `NEXUS_KNOWLEDGE_AUTOEXTRACT=1`, with a visible notice each time a rule is saved. Workspace knowledge is loaded only when the workspace is trusted.

---

# PLAN-01: Safe execution defaults and approval integrity

Implements [SPEC-01](../specs/SPEC-01-safe-execution-defaults.md). Milestone **M1**. Requirements: REQ-SEC-101, 102, 103, 104, 108, 109 and 119; REQ-TUI-102. Decision: DEC-01 option C.

## Preconditions

- PLAN-08 task 1 (test HOME isolation) is merged. Without it, the test changes below write into the real `~/.nexus`.
- Work in a branch or worktree off `main`. Run long suites on a snapshot copy (tasks/lessons.md, 2026-10-13).

## Safe change boundary

These files are in scope:

- `cli/src/core/capabilities.ts`
- `cli/src/core/tool_groups.ts`
- `cli/src/agent.ts` (dispatch gate ~3936-3975; verifier call sites 1602-1630, 3432-3436, 4034, 4067-4090)
- `cli/src/repl.ts`
- `cli/src/sidecar.ts`
- `cli/src/index.ts`
- `cli/src/config.ts`
- `cli/src/types.ts`
- `cli/src/security.ts`
- `cli/src/sandbox.ts`
- `cli/src/core/authority.ts`
- `cli/src/tester.ts` (runner routing only)
- `cli/src/slash/workspace_commands.ts`
- `core/src/runner.rs` (tripwire only)
- `core/src/bin/nexus_tui/{protocol.rs,live_view.rs,live_state.rs}` (posture banner, arrow direction, narrow hints)
- `eval/run.mjs`
- `demo/lib/real-agent-runner.mjs` (`--yes`)

Do not touch the parser, which belongs to PLAN-11, or the runner process registry, which belongs to PLAN-02.

## Tasks (ordered)

| # | Task | Code locations | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Add `EffectClass` type and `effect` field. Classify every built-in capability per SPEC-01 §5.1. MCP and plugin registration defaults to `exec`. Registry validation throws on a missing class. | `core/capabilities.ts:22-45` + each declaration; `mcp.ts` (registration); `plugins.ts` (custom tools) | — |
| 2 | Add `ApprovalPolicy`: `requiresDecision(effect, {mode, trusted, sandbox, egressOrigins})`. Unit test it with the full matrix. | new `cli/src/core/approval_policy.ts` | 1 |
| 3 | Replace `onConfirm && isMutating` with the policy. If no handler is available and a decision is required, return DENIED with reason `DECISION_REQUIRED_NO_OPERATOR`. Egress per-origin memory lives on the agent and is cleared on `/mode` change and on resume. | `agent.ts:3945-3975`; subagent dispatch `agent.ts:5384` | 2 |
| 4 | Replace the `autoApprove` booleans with `HarnessConfig.approvalMode`. Default resolution per DEC-01 C: `--yes`/`NEXUS_APPROVAL_MODE` → explicit, else trusted → auto, else review. CLI flags: `--approve`, `--yes`, `--read-only`, `--mode <m>`. | `config.ts:107`, `types.ts`, `index.ts:93,115`, `repl.ts:69,281,644-648`, `sidecar.ts:53,66,478,638,935` | 3 |
| 5 | Route verifier executions through the policy as `exec`. When not trusted and no prior approval exists, emit the approval with `kind: "verifier"`, the command, and the resolved script body (read `package.json` `scripts.test`, the Makefile `test:` recipe, `Cargo.toml`/`pytest.ini` presence). Cache the approval per (workspace, command, script digest) for the session. | `agent.ts:1602-1630,3432-3436,4034`; `tester.ts:113-136` (add `describeVerifier()`); `approval_review.ts` (new kind) | 3 |
| 6 | `/test` and `nexus eval` use the bridge runner instead of `execSync`. | `tester.ts:143-163`; `repl.ts:1357`; `slash/workspace_commands.ts:160`; `evaluator.ts` | 5 |
| 7 | REPL approval hardening: clear the line buffer, 400 ms grace, `[y/N/d/a]` with empty input = No, confirm for `a`. | `repl.ts:270-276,353,385,497-501` | 4 |
| 8 | Update eval and demo runners to pass `--yes`. Update test fixtures that assumed auto: grep `new InteractiveRepl(`, `SidecarServer(` and `mode:` in `cli/test`. | `eval/run.mjs`, `demo/lib/real-agent-runner.mjs`, `cli/test/**` | 4 |
| 9 | Read-only HOME masking: bwrap `--tmpfs $HOME --ro-bind <ws> <ws>`. Without bwrap, path-confine the allowlisted commands (reject `~`, `$`, absolute paths, and `..` that escapes). | `sandbox.ts:131-181`; `core/authority.ts:44-136` | — |
| 10 | Build the sandbox argv as an array; spawn without a shell. | `sandbox.ts:131-158,181`; caller in `tools.ts` | 9 |
| 11 | Tripwire: shell-words tokenization in TS and Rust; fix false positives; rename in UI and docs; tests for false positives plus documented bypasses. | `security.ts:12-23,78-89`; `runner.rs:64-107` | — |
| 12 | Posture banner: add `posture` to the sidecar `session.state`; render the TUI header line; add a REPL banner line; add `posture` to doctor JSON. | `sidecar.ts`; `protocol.rs`; `live_view.rs` header; `repl.ts` banner; `doctor.ts` | 4 |
| 13 | Approval panel polish: make arrow keys match the button layout; add short-form hints under 60 columns. | `live_state.rs:1329-1335`; `live_view.rs:540-542` | — |
| 14 | Docs: USER_MANUAL approvals/modes, quickstart "review requested actions", ARCHITECTURE §3 controls-and-limits, release notes entry. | docs | 1-13 |

## PR slices

1. **PR-1a** (tasks 1-3): effect classes, policy and gate, with the matrix test. No behaviour change yet: the default is still auto via a temporary constant.
2. **PR-1b** (tasks 4, 8, 12): posture resolution, the DEC-01 C default, fixture updates, banner. This is the behaviour change.
3. **PR-1c** (tasks 5-6): verifier gating and runner routing.
4. **PR-1d** (task 7): REPL approval hardening, with PTY tests.
5. **PR-1e** (tasks 9-11): read-only masking, argv sandbox, tripwire.
6. **PR-1f** (tasks 13-14): TUI polish and docs.

## Tests and fixtures

- **Unit:**
  - `approval_policy.test.ts`: registry × mode × trust matrix; fails on an unclassified capability.
  - `security.test.ts`: tripwire false positives and documented bypasses.
- **Integration:**
  - `verifier_gating.test.ts`: untrusted fixture with a sentinel `scripts.test`, covering ACC-SAFE-09.
  - `readonly_home.test.ts`: fixture HOME with `.ssh/id_rsa`, covering ACC-SAFE-04.
  - `sandbox_quoting.test.ts`, covering ACC-SAFE-05.
- **PTY:**
  - Port `evidence/D_pty/r1_repl.py` and `r1d.py` into `cli/test/repl_approval_e2e.test.ts`, using the existing PTY helper in `cli/test/helpers/fixtures.ts`. Covers ACC-SAFE-03.
  - Add a startup-banner assertion to `tui_surface_e2e`. Covers ACC-SAFE-06.
  - Keep `tui_approval_input_e2e` green (ACC-SAFE-08).
- **Live (M5):** one standalone session per server kind verifies the banner and the first-verifier approval.

## Documentation and packaging

- Add a release-notes entry for the default change and for `--yes` in scripts and CI.
- The quickstart gains a "Trust your own repository" step: `nexus trust .`.

## Rollback

- Each PR reverts independently.
- PR-1b is the only behaviour flip. Reverting it restores the auto default while keeping the classes and gate.
- The `NEXUS_APPROVAL_MODE=auto` escape hatch remains for users after release.

## Definition of done

- ACC-SAFE-01 to ACC-SAFE-10 pass in CI. The PTY tests run in CI (they already run in `linux-x86_64`).
- REQUIREMENTS.md rows REQ-SEC-101/102/103/104/108/109/119 and REQ-TUI-102 show status `tested`, with test references.
- `make test` passes on a clean snapshot.
- The docs checklist items for SPEC-01 are done.

|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `ProcessRegistry` (request_id→pgid, services). Insert after spawn, remove on reap. | `runner.rs:116-167` | — |
| 2 | `cancel` RPC: killpg TERM, then KILL after 2 s, then reply. ESRCH counts as success. | `main.rs:194-203`, `runner.rs` | 1 |
| 3 | Shutdown sweep on stdin EOF, SIGTERM and SIGHUP (`tokio::signal`). `prctl(PR_SET_PDEATHSIG, SIGTERM)` at startup (Linux, `nix` or `libc` crate). | `main.rs` | 1 |
| 4 | Bounded capture: head buffer plus tail ring buffer, and a byte counter in the truncation notice. | `runner.rs:177-193` | — |
| 5 | PTY path kills the pgid. | `runner.rs:319-323` | 1 |
| 6 | `read_file` cap at 8 MB, with an `offset`/`length` paging hint in the error. Same for `batch_read`. | `file_ops.rs:205-277`; capability schema in `capabilities.ts` | — |
| 7 | Clamp `timeout_secs` to `NEXUS_MAX_TOOL_TIMEOUT_SECS` (default 1800) and tell the model it was clamped. | `tools.ts` (args), `runner.rs` | — |

| 13 | Docs: USER_MANUAL cancellation section; ARCHITECTURE runner section; residual risk of `setsid` escape without the sandbox. | docs | all |

1. **PR-2a** (tasks 1-5, Rust only). Registry, cancel RPC, shutdown sweep, bounded capture. Rust unit tests in `runner.rs` follow the style of the existing descendant test (`runner.rs:479-500`).
2. **PR-2b** (tasks 8-9). Bridge and agent plumbing, plus the ACC-PROC PTY tests.
3. **PR-2c** (tasks 6, 7, 10). Read cap, timeout clamp, services.
4. **PR-2d** (tasks 11-13). TUI feedback, notification gating, docs.

## Tests

- **Rust:**
  - `cancel_kills_group`
  - `shutdown_on_eof_kills_all`
  - `pdeathsig_sweeps` (spawn harness-core under a parent that exits)
  - `bounded_capture_400mb`, which measures RSS through `/proc/self/status`

- The registry and sweep are additive.

- ACC-PROC-01 to ACC-PROC-08 pass.
- Ledger rows updated.
- The ISSUE12 EXEC-009 and SUBP-004/005 historical rows are annotated as superseded by REQ-AGT-109 and REQ-SEC-106 (PLAN-09).

- **Requirements:** REQ-SEC-110 through REQ-SEC-118, and REQ-PRV-108.

- `cli/src/config.ts`
- `cli/src/client.ts` (env reads only)

- `cli/src/core/provider_recovery.ts` (env reads)

| 6 | Trust-gate workspace skill roots and workspace `knowledge.json`. `/skills` lists untrusted entries as such. `activate_skill` on an untrusted skill is refused with a hint. Injected blocks are annotated with source and trust state (partial CTX-001). | `skills.ts:31-33`; `knowledge.ts`; `agent.ts:3301,3789`; `slash/extension_commands.ts` | — |

| 10 | Protected paths: match `.env*`, check the canonical target and case-insensitive variants, and apply the check on every read tool. Document that it is advisory for `run_command`. | `security.ts:25-32,91-108`; `tools.ts:446-469` | — |

## PR slices

| PR | Tasks | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| PR-3a | 1-3 | Config layering. Regression test from `evidence/prv/tls.mts`. |
| PR-3b | 4, 9 | Locality and search_web. |
| PR-3c | 5 | SSRF-safe fetch. |
| PR-3d | 6-7 | Skills and knowledge trust. |
| PR-3e | 8, 10 | Plugins, EXT-004 and protected paths. |
| PR-3f | 11 | Docs. |

## Tests

- **`project_env_allowlist.test.ts`**: one case per denied class: `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, `HOME`, `LOCAL_LLM_API_KEY`, `LOCAL_LLM_TIMEOUT_MS`, `LOCAL_LLM_FALLBACK_ENDPOINTS`. Also the TLS mock check (ACC-TRUST-01). The self-signed cert is generated at test time with `openssl` or `node:crypto` (`selfsigned` is not needed: use `generateKeyPairSync` plus a pre-made fixture cert under `cli/test/fixtures/tls/`).
- **`egress.test.ts`**: extend with the ACC-TRUST-02 table.
- **`fetch_web_ssrf.test.ts`**: local HTTP server plus a redirector (ACC-TRUST-03).
- **`workspace_trust.test.ts`**: extend for skills and knowledge (ACC-TRUST-04/05).
- **`plugins_dirs.test.ts`**: sentinel plugin (ACC-TRUST-06).
- **`ext004_audit.test.ts`** (ACC-TRUST-07).
- **`search_web.test.ts`** (ACC-TRUST-08).
- **`security.test.ts`**: protected-path cases (ACC-TRUST-09).

## Migration and rollback

Migration: the release notes list the moved keys. Doctor tells users exactly which project keys were ignored, and where to put each one.

Rollback per PR:

- PR-3a is the riskiest, because it touches many env reads. Keep a temporary `NEXUS_LEGACY_PROJECT_ENV=1` escape hatch for one RC cycle only, then remove it before v1.0.0 GA.

- ACC-TRUST-01 to ACC-TRUST-09 pass.
- `grep -n "override: *true" cli/src/config.ts` returns nothing.
- Ledger rows are updated, and the DEC-04 disposition is reflected in REQUIREMENTS §2.

This plan implements [SPEC-04](../specs/SPEC-04-continuity-and-durable-work.md) in milestone **M3**.

- Requirements: REQ-AGT-101 to 108, 110, and 111 (partial).
- Decision: DEC-03 (team/operation ship as experimental).

- `cli/src/core/app.ts:174-229`
- `cli/src/index.ts:176` and the `--resume` handling

- `cli/src/core/operation_runner.ts:95-137,559,651-663`

- `cli/src/core/objective.ts` (attempt counter)
- `cli/src/core/state.ts` (failure reporting)
- `docs/EXECUTION_CONVERGENCE.md`, `docs/COMPACTION_AND_CONTINUITY.md`

## Tasks

| # | Task | Code locations | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `run(prompt, {resume})` skips `resetConversation` and keeps the objective; `runTask` takes the recovered taskId; `--resume` with no id resolves the latest task in the workspace, otherwise exits 2 with guidance. | `agent.ts:5236`; `app.ts:174-177`; `index.ts:176`; `state.ts` (`listTasks` by workspace) | — |
| 2 | Add a `durable` property and replace the depth gates. Classify each site in the PR description (one line each). | `agent.ts:1136-1139,1148,1489-1501,1587-1590,3081,3127,4034,4389`; `AgentWorkUnitExecutor` | — |
| 3 | Give work units an objective ledger keyed by unit id; offer `update_requirements`/`read_objective` to implementer and tester roles. | `agent.ts`, `objective.ts`, `team.ts` | 2 |
| 4 | Persist execution tracking and the change baseline for durable units, and restore them on resume. | `execution_tracking.ts` (`fresh()` call sites), `objective.ts trackingOf` | 2 |
| 5 | Subagent stats merge; `recordFindings` counts requests; no task record when not durable. | `agent.ts:1869,2863,5298-5431` | 2 |
| 6 | Call `measureAdmission` in the subagent loop and make the offered tool set equal the accepted set. Document the remaining divergences. | `agent.ts:5298-5431` | 5 |
| 7 | Fix the obligation write to call `setUnverifiedChanges` once and count once. | `agent.ts:3610-3641` | — |
| 8 | Wrap `runTurn` and build an `UNHANDLED_ERROR` result in-agent; final checkpoint; cancel the steering and compaction queues with notices. | `agent.ts:4254-4995`; `turn.ts:444-460`; `app.ts:229` | — |
| 9 | Stagnation rule for unknown state identity (distinct successful writes count as progress), plus the inverse test. | `execution_tracking.ts evaluateStep` | — |
| 10 | Role-aware unit classification: a NOT_REQUIRED result from an implementer or tester unit becomes BLOCKED(no_change); give the 10k-transition stop real options. | `operation_runner.ts:95-137,651-663` | — |
| 11 | Make the attempt counter monotonic. | `objective.ts recordAttempt` | — |
| 12 | Route all durable-write failures through `reportPersistenceFailure`. | `agent.ts:1182-1185,3836-3867,4022-4058,4240-4243` | — |
| 13 | Persistence cost measurement harness (ACC-CONT-08). If over threshold, open a follow-up for the split-record schema (SPEC-04 §3.7 / SPEC-08). | new `cli/test/perf/persistence_cost.bench.ts` (not in the default suite) | — |
| 14 | Experimental labels for `/team` and `nexus operation` in help and docs; correct the team-steps doc; describe compaction behaviour for work units. | `index.ts`, slash catalog, `EXECUTION_CONVERGENCE.md:117-118`, `COMPACTION_AND_CONTINUITY.md` | 2 |

## PR slices

| PR | Tasks | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| PR-4a | 1 | Resume fix. This is a blocker; land it first. |
| PR-4b | 2, 4 | Durability property and persisted tracking. Blocker AGT-02a. |
| PR-4c | 3, 10 | Unit ledger and outcome semantics. |
| PR-4d | 5, 6, 7 | Subagent hygiene. |
| PR-4e | 8, 12 | Error path and failure reporting. |
| PR-4f | 9, 11, 13, 14 | Stagnation, counter, measurement and docs. |

## Tests

- Extend `durable_continuity.test.ts` with the resume-conversation assertion and the `latest` case (ACC-CONT-01/02). Port the R2 case from `evidence/repro/agt_repro.test.ts`.
- Use the `operationRig` with a small `contextLimit`, SIGKILL, then resume. Assert the archive lines and `read_archive` (ACC-CONT-03), plus loop persistence (ACC-CONT-04).
- R4 port for accounting and records (ACC-CONT-05).
- Fault injection: stub `admitContext` to throw (ACC-CONT-06).
- `team_convergence.test.ts`: an implementer that replies with prose only (ACC-CONT-07).
- `execution_tracking.test.ts`: unknown-identity cases (ACC-CONT-09).
- **Live (M5):** one long task with at least 60 steps and at least 2 compactions on the RC, run independently (ACC-CONT-10).

## Rollback

Each PR stands alone. PR-4b changes durable behaviour for units; reverting it restores the alpha.2 semantics. No schema change unless task 13 triggers one.

## Definition of done

- ACC-CONT-01 to 09 pass in CI.
- ACC-CONT-10 is recorded in M5.
- Ledger rows are updated.
- The doc corrections are merged.

# PLAN-07: Supply chain, compliance and release engineering

This plan implements [SPEC-07](../specs/SPEC-07-supply-chain-and-release-engineering.md). It belongs to milestone **M2**.

- Requirements: REQ-REL-107 to REQ-REL-114.
- Decisions: DEC-09, DEC-10.

## Safe change boundary

- `scripts/package-linux.sh`, `scripts/generate_sbom.sh`, `scripts/security_gates.sh`, `scripts/audit_rust_deps.py`
- `.github/workflows/{ci,release}.yml`, `.gitlab-ci.yml`
- `Makefile`
- new `about.toml`, `about.hbs`, `deny.toml`, `rust-toolchain.toml`
- `core/Cargo.toml` (`rust-version`)
- `cli/package.json` (`engines`)
- `.gitignore`, `cli/dist` (untrack)
- new `SECURITY.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`
- `docs/releases/`

## Tasks

| # | Task | Code locations | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Add `rust-toolchain.toml` pinned to the current stable (1.95.0 at audit time), set `rust-version` in Cargo.toml, and add `"engines": {"node": ">=20"}`. | root, `core/Cargo.toml`, `cli/package.json` | — |
| 2 | Third-party notices: install cargo-about and the npm license checker in CI. Use `about.toml` with an allowlist (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-2/3, ISC, Unicode-3.0, Zlib, MPL-2.0 only if reviewed). Have `package-linux.sh` write `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt` and upload it as an asset. | `package-linux.sh:22`; `release.yml` | 1 |
| 3 | `cargo deny check licenses advisories` in CI. Make `security_gates.sh` fail if `cargo-audit`/`cargo-deny` is missing, and delete `audit_rust_deps.py`. | `security_gates.sh:84-97`; `ci.yml`; `release.yml` | 1 |
| 4 | Build the SBOM from lockfiles with cyclonedx-npm and cargo-cyclonedx, merge and validate, and attach it to the release. Replace `generate_sbom.sh` and update `make sbom`. | `scripts/generate_sbom.sh`; `Makefile`; `release.yml` | — |
| 5 | Add provenance with `actions/attest-build-provenance` on the tarball and SHA256SUMS, and upload `install.sh` as a release asset. The installer optionally runs `gh attestation verify` when `gh` is available. | `release.yml:44-48`; `install.sh` | — |
| 6 | Add a CI matrix for Node 20/22/24 (tests). Packaging stays on Node 20. Pin the cargo-audit version. | `ci.yml` | 1 |
| 7 | Untrack `cli/dist`: `git rm -r --cached cli/dist`, add it to `.gitignore`, and check that the docs and `make build` cover it. Confirm `harness.sh` still errors helpfully when dist is missing. | `.gitignore`; `harness.sh`; docs | — |
| 8 | Delete `.gitlab-ci.yml`. Remove tracked `*.pyc` and ignore them. Point `make verify-reproducibility` at `package-linux.sh` run twice with mktemp and cmp. | `.gitlab-ci.yml`; `experiments/context-validation-2026-10-04/harness/__pycache__`; `Makefile:36-45` | — |
| 9 | Write `SECURITY.md` (private reporting via GitHub Security Advisories, supported versions, 7-day acknowledgement target) and `CHANGELOG.md` (back-filled from docs/releases). Set the release body from `docs/releases/<tag>.md` (`body_path`), and fail if that file is missing. | root; `release.yml` | — |
| 10 | Cross-runner reproducibility: a workflow_dispatch job builds on ubuntu-22.04 and ubuntu-24.04 with the pinned toolchain and compares the outputs. Run it once for the RC. | new `.github/workflows/repro.yml` | 1 |

## PR slices

| PR | Tasks |
|---|---|
| PR-7a | 1, 6, 8 |
| PR-7b | 2, 3 (notices and gates) |
| PR-7c | 4, 5 (SBOM and provenance) |
| PR-7d | 7 (dist untrack, isolated because the diff is large) |
| PR-7e | 9, 10 |

## Tests

- **ACC-SUP-01.** Add `scripts/check_notices.mjs`. It takes `cargo metadata --locked --format-version 1` (filtered to the dependency closure of the `harness-core` and `nexus-tui` targets) plus `npm ls --omit=dev --all --json`, and checks that every listed package appears in the notices file.
- **ACC-SUP-02.** Run `cyclonedx validate` in release.
- **ACC-SUP-03.** Run `gh attestation verify` in a post-release verification job against the published asset.
- **ACC-SUP-04.** Add a negative test to `security_gates.test.ts`: with `PATH` stripped of cargo-audit, the gate exits non-zero.
- **ACC-SUP-05 to ACC-SUP-08.** These are observed in CI or the repo state.

## Rollback

Workflow changes revert per PR. Untracking dist is reversible with `git add -f`.

## Definition of done

- ACC-SUP-01 to ACC-SUP-08 pass for the RC.
- The release assets are: tarball, SHA256SUMS, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt, the SBOM, install.sh, and the attestation.

| PR | Tasks | Milestone |
|---|---|---|
| PR-8a | 1 | M0, merge first |

| PR-8d | 7, 9 | M4 |
| PR-8e | 8, 10 | M4 |

| Acceptance | Test |
|---|---|
| ACC-PER-01 | `permissions.test.ts`, run under `process.umask(0o002)` |
| ACC-PER-02 | `retention.test.ts`, with seeded records and a session-listing time budget |

  ```

# PLAN-09: Requirements governance and documentation truth

This plan implements [SPEC-09](../specs/SPEC-09-requirements-governance-and-docs.md).

| | |
|---|---|
| Milestones | **M0** (ledger checker, historical banners). **M6** (final doc sign-off). Doc fixes land with each feature PR. |
| Requirements | REQ-OPS-101, REQ-OPS-102, REQ-OPS-103, REQ-DX-105, REQ-DX-106, REQ-AGT-110 |
| Decision | DEC-04 |

## Tasks

| # | Task | Location | Milestone |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Write `scripts/check_requirements.mjs`. It parses the REQUIREMENTS.md tables. For each BLOCKER or RELEASE-REQUIRED row it requires SPEC, PLAN and ACC references, and test references whose substring exists in `cli/test`, `core` or `scripts`. It fails on a missing reference and writes a summary table. Run it in `ci.yml`. In M0 it runs in **report mode**: a row whose status is `open` passes as long as it has its SPEC, PLAN and ACC links. From M6 it runs in **enforce mode**: every row must be at least `tested`. | new script; `ci.yml` | M0 |
| 2 | Add a HISTORICAL banner to `docs/ISSUE12_*.md`, `docs/PHASE*.md`, `docs/WP*.md`, `docs/CLOUDFLARE_CONTEST_CRITICAL_PATH_ASSESSMENT.md`, and the `docs/reviews/*` older than 2026-10-14. The banner text is "Historical record. Current requirements: docs/v1.0.0/REQUIREMENTS.md." | docs | M0 |
| 3 | Create the GitHub milestone `v1.0.0` and one issue per PLAN PR slice, each linked to its ledger IDs. Because this changes GitHub state, it is an **owner-approved action** in the implementation phase. | GitHub | M0 |
| 4 | Fix documentation as part of each feature PR, following the SPEC-09 §3.2 checklist. Run a final pass before the RC. | docs | M1–M6 |
| 5 | Remove the parity claim, homelab identifiers, and the `file:///` link. Correct the ARCHITECTURE controls-and-limits section. | `USER_MANUAL.md:3`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `MCP_GUIDE.md`, `CLOUD_PROVIDERS.md` | M0 (cheap, standalone) |
| 6 | Arrange the independent acceptance of continuity, compaction and truncation recovery (owner action X5). The reviewer receives SPEC-04 §1–2, ACC-CONT-01..10, and the RC build. Their report goes to `docs/reviews/`. | — | M5 |
| 7 | In M6, update REQUIREMENTS.md statuses with the RC commit, and switch the checker to enforce mode. | ledger | M6 |

## PR slices

- **PR-9a (M0).** Tasks 1, 2 and 5.
- Task 4 has no PR of its own: its changes ride with the feature PRs.
- **PR-9b (M6).** Task 7.

## Tests

- **ACC-GOV-01.** The checker has a fixture ledger containing one row whose test name is missing. The checker must exit non-zero on it.
- **ACC-GOV-04.** A grep step in CI.

## Definition of done

ACC-GOV-01 through ACC-GOV-06 pass.

| Work | Estimate | Main uncertainty |

Implements [SPEC-11](../specs/SPEC-11-verification-and-tool-call-integrity.md). Parser and binding work is milestone **M1**. The rest is **M3**.

- **Requirements:** REQ-AGT-112 to REQ-AGT-119.

- `cli/src/parser.ts`
- `cli/src/fewshots.ts`
- `cli/src/tester.ts`
- `cli/src/tools.ts:588-610`

## Tasks

| # | Task | Code locations | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `parseModelResponse(reply, {nativeTools})`. Native connections parse native `tool_calls` only. Text connections accept `<tool_call>` blocks, or a sole fenced call. Prose JSON is never parsed. Add a `nativeTools` capability per protocol and connection (Chat Completions sends `tools` and the server accepts them; Responses and Anthropic are always native). | `parser.ts:319-434`; `client.ts` (capability); `agent.ts:4701` | — |
| 2 | Reasoning stripping handles a lone `</think>` (everything before it is reasoning), an unclosed `<think>` (everything after it is reasoning), `<reasoning>`, and `reasoning_content`. | `parser.ts:320-332` | — |
| 3 | Few-shots: for native connections, drop the fenced text-call exemplars. Text connections keep only the accepted format. | `fewshots.ts:18-56` | 1 |
| 4 | Validate the shape of malformed native `tool_calls`. Drop invalid entries and give the model a notice. Unknown names produce a notice, not a dispatch. | `parser.ts:336-345` | 1 |
| 5 | `repairJson` returns its repair class. Dispatch rejects a `structural` repair for `write_workspace`/`exec`. Depends on PLAN-01 task 1 (effect classes). | `parser.ts:189-231`; dispatch | 1 |
| 6 | Binding uses path-token matching (`isVerifierDeliverableBound`). A test-file change binds only when that file's tests ran. | `tester.ts:356-360` | — |
| 7 | Per-runner result parsers (node:test, jest, vitest, mocha, pytest, cargo, go) returning executed/skipped counts. A zero-executed pass gives UNVERIFIED/NO_TESTS_EXECUTED and keeps the obligation. | `tester.ts:263-282`; `agent.ts:3520,5126-5135` | — |

| 9 | Conservative token estimator, plus `/tokenize` on llama.cpp and vLLM when available. Calibration fixture of reference counts, generated once with a pinned tokenizer and committed as JSON. | `tokens.ts:5-26`; `agent.ts:2247-2300` | PLAN-05 task 1 |
| 10 | Reviewer and researcher units get a read-only tool set, enforced from `roles.ts recommendedTools`. | `core/roles.ts:20-76`; `team.ts` | — |
| 11 | Experimental labels for `nexus eval` and `/tdd`. `nexus eval` runs in a worktree (shared with PLAN-10 task 10). | `index.ts`; slash catalog; `evaluator.ts:128` | — |
| 12 | Polish: clipboard args (`execFileSync(cmd,args)`), image cap of 20 MB with no SVG, hunk path parsing from the `---`/`+++` headers. | `clipboard.ts:21-27`; `image.ts:25-74`; `stager.ts:45-47` | — |

|---|---|---|---|
| PR-11a | 1–4 | M1 | Parser; blocker VER-02/03 |

| PR-11c | 5, 8 | M3 | |
| PR-11d | 9 | M3 | |
| PR-11e | 10–12 | M3 | |

| Acceptance | Test |
|---|---|
| ACC-VER-01, ACC-VER-02, ACC-VER-06 | Port `evidence/a2probe/parser_probe.ts` into `cli/test/parser_safety.test.ts` |
| ACC-VER-03, ACC-VER-04, ACC-VER-05 | Port `tester_probe.ts` into `verification_binding.test.ts` |
| ACC-VER-07 | `tokens.test.ts` with the calibration fixture |
| ACC-VER-09 | Re-run the historical false-VERIFIED repro: `docs/reviews/evidence/qualification_2026-10-12/repro/repro_false_verified.test.ts`. Copy it into `cli/test/` so it runs in CI. |

The parser change could reduce tool-call success on servers that only emit text calls. Mitigations:

+## 2. Architecture / data-flow notes

+- `AutonomousAgent.runTurn` (agent.ts:4254-4995) is the single main loop. Per step: steering drain (4450) -> capability refresh (4555) -> `admitWithFindings` (compaction ladder + model-written findings, 2767) -> `measureAdmission` (provider token count, 2237) -> `ProviderRecoveryController.run` around streaming inference (4614) -> parse -> tool dispatch (parallel only if every call is in `READ_ONLY_TOOLS`, 4800; else sequential with approval) -> `observe` into `ExecutionTracker` -> `endStep` (progress evaluation + durable `persistProgress`).

+- Stop conditions: `task_completed` success, FINAL_TEXT (after up to `maxCompletionNudges`=2 nudges while requirements are open), cancellation (AbortController; in-flight tool awaited), inference failure after recovery, context admission refusal (BLOCKED), persistence failure, stagnation (`stagnationSteps`=12 consecutive no-progress steps, or a repeated loop after `maxRecoveries`=2 notes), operator step/time budgets (default +Infinity, types.ts:127-133), `--no-continuation` (maxSteps, default 30, as a hard LIMIT_REACHED).
+- Default turn has **no cumulative step ceiling**: `maxSteps`=30 is a segment (durable checkpoint) only (agent.ts:4379-4381, 4435). Confirmed.

+- Outcome derivation is centralised in `buildTurnResult` (5007-5173) with invariants in `assertTurnResultInvariants` (turn.ts:318). Exit codes: 0 VERIFIED/NOT_REQUIRED, 2 REGRESSION_FREE/UNVERIFIED, 130 interrupted, 1 otherwise.

+- Verification gate lives in the `task_completed` handler (3345-3571): open/blocked requirements refuse; configured or discovered verifier runs; prior FAILED on identical inputs is not rerun; discovered-verifier pass is VERIFIED only with fail-before/pass-after independence.

+- Durable state: `~/.nexus/tasks/<task>.json` written via full load+redact+atomic write on every progress event (state.ts recordProgress/recordOperationStart/End). Compaction originals go to `<task>.history.jsonl` before the record names the compaction.

+- Three agent kinds share the class: depth 0 (interactive/run; durable, has objective ledger), depth 1 work units (`AgentWorkUnitExecutor`, durable, resumed from task state, **no objective ledger**), depth 1/2 in-turn subagents (`runSubagent`, separate loop, declared non-durable).

+## 5. Strengths (with evidence)

+- No default cumulative step ceiling: `DEFAULT_CONTINUATION.maxTotalSteps/maxTurnMinutes = +Infinity` (types.ts:127-133); `maxSteps` is a segment/checkpoint (agent.ts:4379-4381, 4435-4445). Step-position notices only appear under an operator-set limit (`stepPosition`, 766; `stepNotedContent` 2932-2933). Subagents have no step allowance; model-supplied `max_steps` ignored (3584-3585). Recovery/iteration bounds that remain (provider `maxIterations` 1000, operation runner 10 000, compaction attempts 5) are resource-safety valves with explicit reasons, not completion substitutes.

+- Stagnation is evidence-based (action/outcome/state triples with volatile-token normalization, polls vs loops, compaction-reacquisition excluded as thrash), persisted in the objective ledger across compaction/turns/restart for depth-0 (execution_tracking.ts; objective.ts `trackingOf`).

+- Outcome honesty: `buildTurnResult` is the single derivation; invariants forbid VERIFIED/REGRESSION_FREE without PASSED evidence and NOT_REQUIRED with pending changes (turn.ts:318-351). Discovered-verifier passes need fail-before/pass-after independence for VERIFIED (agent.ts:3447, 5136-5145); non-covering passes are REGRESSION_FREE (5126-5135); read-only answers resting on compacted-away output are UNVERIFIED/CONTEXT_EVIDENCE_NOT_RETAINED (5165-5171). `verified` requirements must bind a passing, unfiltered, deliverable-bound, independent run (objective.ts applyRequirementUpdates).

+- Failed mutating commands still create the obligation (R1: `exit 3` after modifying a file → `pending=true`, UNVERIFIED) because run_command reports `success` with an exit_code body and the spine's mutation hook fires on tool success.

+- Cancellation: authority event with per-phase interruption records; no new dispatch after abort; undispatched calls get synthetic tool results so history stays well-formed (4359-4372, 4737-4741, 4841-4850).
+- Provider recovery separates waiting/probing from replay; UNKNOWN execution replayed at most `maxUnknownReplays` after a probe; NOT_EXECUTED can yield to the scheduler (provider_recovery.ts).
+- Compaction commit protocol for depth-0 (archive → switch → records; non-durable compaction stops the turn) is implemented as documented (agent.ts:3070-3153).
+- Steering: queued, applied once at step boundaries, never dropped silently (cancelled + reported), survives restore (1935-1973, 1553-1557).
+- Truncated replies (finish_reason=length) get one in-turn retry with a precise notice; second in a row ends the turn (4672-4683).

+## 2. Architecture and data flow
+- **Verifier selection.** There are two selectors that disagree.

+  - `discoverVerifier` (tester.ts:109-138) needs repository evidence and is used for the completion oracle, the baseline and the prompt. Its order is: Makefile `^test:` → `make test`; Cargo.toml / core/Cargo.toml → `cargo test`; package.json `scripts.test` (not "no test specified") → `npm test` (also `npm --prefix cli test`); pyproject/setup.py → `pytest`; go.mod → `go test ./...`; `test_*.py` in tests/, test/ or the root → `python3 -m unittest discover`; otherwise null (NO_APPLICABLE_VERIFIER → UNVERIFIED).

+  - `detectTestCommand` (tester.ts:21-78) uses a looser Makefile check (`includes("test:")`) and falls back to `npm test`. It is used by the `run_tests` tool (tools.ts:589), the TDD synthesizer (synthesizer.ts:65), `nexus eval` and `/test` (via runTestSuite).

+- **Pass/fail.** `runTestSuiteWithExecutor` sets success only when the Rust runner envelope has `exit_code === 0 && !timed_out`. Unknown executor output means not success (tester.ts:179-193). Output scraping is used only for (a) `hasExecutedTests`, which decides whether tests ran, and (b) `isVerifierDeliverableBound`, which decides whether the run covers the change.
+- **Outcome derivation** (agent.ts:5100-5150):
+  - pending changes, verifier FAILED or TIMED_OUT → NOT_ESTABLISHED
+  - verifier PASSED and not deliverable-bound → REGRESSION_FREE
+  - discovered verifier, bound, not independent → REGRESSION_FREE
+  - configured verifier and bound, or discovered and bound and independent (fail-before/pass-after with Nexus's own test edits set aside, agent.ts:1622-1638) → VERIFIED

+- **Timeouts.** The oracle and the baseline use `verifierTimeoutSecs`, default 300 s (agent.ts:149), enforced by the runner. A timeout is never a pass (tester.ts:193; verifier_timeout.test.ts passes). The `run_tests` tool hard-codes 120 s (tools.ts:594). `/test` and `nexus eval` use host `execSync` with a 120 s limit, which blocks the event loop (tester.ts:151-156).

+- **Trust boundary.** Verifier commands run repository-defined code: Makefile recipes, package.json scripts, build.rs, conftest.py. They run through `bridge.executeTool("run_command")` directly, so the dispatch approval gate (agent.ts:3947) never sees them. The sandbox applies only if `--sandbox`/read-only is set (tools.ts:755). No workspace-trust check applies.
+- **Parser.** `parseModelResponse` (parser.ts:307) handles, in order:
+  1. `<think>`/`<thought>` stripping (needs both tags)
+  2. native `tool_calls` (no validation)
+  3. `<tool_call>` XML
+  4. ```json code blocks
+  5. any balanced `{…}` in prose whose `name`/`tool`/`action` is an offered tool

+  `repairJson` adds trailing-comma, unquoted-key, Python-literal, single-quote and bracket/quote-closing repairs. Truncated replies (finish_reason=length) are refused upstream in client.ts:1177-1183 and 1461, and agent.ts:4670-4685 asks the model to write the content in parts.

+- **Token accounting.** Exact counts come only from a connection that advertises `tokenize` (agent.ts:2247). Otherwise the regex estimator in tokens.ts is the admission basis. Strict counting is opt-in and refuses unmeasured requests. `estimateScale` calibrates estimates only after a measured count.

Everything else (TLS/Node env, timeouts, recovery policy, LOCAL_LLM_ENDPOINT/FALLBACKS, provider key env vars) reads live `process.env`.

+- Two connection kinds: (a) legacy "appliance/endpoint" path (no provider id): OpenAI Chat Completions, `/v1` appended, fallback list, `X-Task-Class`, gateway token file / config.env key scoped by origin (client.ts:123-133), no receipts, no spending limits; (b) provider connections (providers.ts:46-116): openrouter, openai (Responses), anthropic (Messages), compatible, chatgpt (unofficial OAuth), copilot (unofficial OAuth); pinned endpoint, own key only, `redirect:"error"`, receipts in `<ws>/.nexus/inference_receipts.jsonl`, spending limits (usage.ts).

+## 2. Architecture / data-flow notes

+- Model tool call -> `agent.dispatchToolCall` (agent.ts:3880). Vault `restore()` puts real secrets back into args for non-egress tools (agent.ts:3899-3906). Flight recorder logs args. The **approval gate runs only when an `onConfirm` handler exists and the capability is `mutating`** (agent.ts:3946-3947). The handler auto-approves unless `--approve` / `/mode review` is set: repl.ts:69,281; index.ts:93,115; sidecar.ts:935.

+- Non-mutating, so never prompted even in review mode: fetch_web, search_web, browser_navigate, browser_click, browser_screenshot, spawn_subagent, activate_skill, every read/search tool (capabilities.ts:514,576,772,824,1164,1215).

+- `ExecutionSpine` hands off to the authority engine (authority.ts). With no grants it admits everything at "workspace" scope (authority.ts:264), then lexically confines path args (authority.ts:318-334). Then `RustCoreBridge.executeTool` (tools.ts:432) runs the TS checks: substring command denylist, name-pattern protected paths, read-only allowlist, and optional bwrap/docker wrap. Then JSON-RPC to `harness-core rpc`, which runs every request on a blocking thread with no concurrency limit (main.rs:194-203).

+- Rust boundary: `resolve_safe_path` does lexical normalisation plus canonicalize of the target or nearest existing ancestor (file_ops.rs:731-791). Reads and writes recheck via `/proc/self/fd` (file_ops.rs:59-87). `run_command` is `bash -c <string>` with only a cwd jail (runner.rs:116-157). The shell itself is unconfined unless the sandbox is enabled.
+- Trust boundaries:
+  - Workspace MCP configs and plugin JS are gated by `~/.config/nexus/trusted_workspaces.json` (workspace_trust.ts:35).
+  - Workspace **skills are not gated**. They are loaded from `./skills`, `./.nexus/skills` and `./.claude/skills` (skills.ts:31-33) and injected into the system prompt (agent.ts:3301).
+  - `.nexus-security.json` is read from the untrusted workspace (security.ts:48). It can only add entries, except that `allowedDomains` narrows egress and `allowExternalSymlinks` is never consumed.
+- Persistence:
+  - Sessions and tasks: `~/.nexus/{sessions,tasks}/<id>.json` via `writeFileDurably`. This is a temp file + rename with mode 0600; fsync only inside `withDurableSync` (durable_file.ts:49-74).
+  - Schema: `schemaVersion` = 1. Future versions fail closed. Legacy v0 is migrated on load (state.ts:425-431, 823-858).
+  - Compaction archive: `.history.jsonl` lines appended with fsync.
+  - Flight logs: `<workspace>/.nexus/flights/*.flightlog`, appendFileSync with default mode.
+  - Checkpoints: `~/.nexus/checkpoints/<hash>/`, writeFileSync with default mode, plus git refs `refs/nexus/checkpoints/*`.
+  - Audit: `~/.nexus/audit.log`. REPL history: `~/.nexus_history`.

+## 5. Strengths (with evidence)

+- The Rust file-tool jail is sound against `..`, absolute paths, symlinked files and dirs, and symlinked parents of new files (R1). There is a descriptor-level recheck via `/proc/self/fd` after open (file_ops.rs:59-87). Atomic temp+rename writes keep permissions, refuse read-only files, and write hard-linked files in place (file_ops.rs:101-188).
+- `delete_file` refuses the workspace root and `.git` on both the canonical and lexical path (file_ops.rs:705-716). TS pre-check: tools.ts:43-50.
+- Commands run in their own process group, and timeout uses killpg TERM then KILL (runner.rs:164-167, 245-264). There is a test for descendants (runner.rs:479-500).

+- No shell is used for git (git2) or for worktree ops (execFileSync argv). MCP children get an env allowlist (mcp.ts:56-77). Workspace MCP and plugins require explicit trust, and never get it in read-only mode (workspace_trust.ts:35-53, mcp.ts:509-531).

+- Session state: schema version with fail-closed on future versions, legacy migration, identity and workspace binding on load, redaction before persist, and a fsync'd append-only compaction archive with a commit protocol (state.ts:338-460; durable_file.ts). The trust store is written atomically with 0600/0700 (workspace_trust.ts:71-76).
+- `safe_fs.ts` (doctor --fix) is a careful O_NOFOLLOW + fd-verified mutation design.
+- The read-only sandbox probe exercises the real mount boundary instead of trusting that bwrap is present (sandbox.ts:55-73).

# Nexus Code v1.0.0: requirement ledger

This is the authoritative v1 ledger (REQ-OPS-101). It supersedes the Issue #12 matrices (`docs/ISSUE12_*.md`) and the phase and work-package documents, which become historical records. All historical commitments are carried forward in §2. None are silently dropped. Each one is either retained, superseded or descoped, with a written disposition.

**Tested revision for every status below:** `db1ca55` (main, `v0.1.0-alpha.2-2-gdb1ca55`), audited 2026-10-14.

## 1. Legend

### Status ladder

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `open` | Not implemented, or contradicted at HEAD. |
| `partial` | Partly implemented, or implemented with a known defect. |
| `implemented` | Present in source. Not proven by an automated test of this requirement. |
| `tested` | An automated test exercises it and passes at the tested revision (baseline: 905/905 CLI, 266/266 Rust). |
| `visually-accepted` | A human or independent PTY review accepted the rendered behaviour. |
| `product-qualified` | Passed the v1 qualification in ACCEPTANCE.md on the RC. **No requirement holds this status today.** |

Independent acceptance is recorded separately in the "Indep." column: **Y** = an independent review accepted it; **N** = self-assessed only; **—** = not applicable.

### Release classes

| Class | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **B** | BLOCKER. v1.0.0 cannot ship without it. |
| **RR** | Release-required. Must be done for v1.0.0; it is not a safety or workflow blocker on its own, but the release gate checks it. |
| **P** | Post-v1. |
| **K** | Keep: already met; protected by regression tests. |

### Evidence labels

| Label | Kind of evidence |
|---|---|
| SRC | source inspection |
| TEST | automated test |
| RT | live runtime observation (including PTY) |
| MEAS | measurement |
| DOC | documentation claim |
| HIST | historical or reported evidence |
| INF | inference |
| UNV | unknown or unverified |

### Links

- Findings are defined in [AUDIT.md](AUDIT.md).
- Specs are in [specs/](specs/), plans in [plans/](plans/), acceptance IDs in [ACCEPTANCE.md](ACCEPTANCE.md).

## 2. Carried-over commitments (REQ-*-0xx)

### 2.1 Retained commitments (already met or partly met; must not regress)

| ID | Source | Requirement | Location | Evidence @db1ca55 | Status | Indep. | Open risk | Acceptance | Class | Links |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| REQ-AGT-001 | COMPACTION_AND_CONTINUITY §A; operator directive | No default cumulative step or time ceiling. Turns end on completion, cancel, demonstrated stagnation, actionable failure or an operator-set budget. Resource-safety valves (provider iterations, 10k scheduler transitions, 5 compaction attempts) are allowed and labelled. | `types.ts:127-133`; `agent.ts:4379-4445` | TEST + SRC (A §5) | tested | N | Docs overstate the team "15-step cap" (AGT-07) | ACC-CONT-04, ACC-QUAL-T3 | K | SPEC-04 |

This is the authoritative v1 ledger (REQ-OPS-101). It supersedes the Issue #12 matrices (`docs/ISSUE12_*.md`) and the phase and work-package documents, which become historical records. All historical commitments are carried forward in §2. None are silently dropped. Each one is either retained, superseded or descoped, with a written disposition.

**Tested revision for every status below:** `db1ca55` (main, `v0.1.0-alpha.2-2-gdb1ca55`), audited 2026-10-14.

## 1. Legend

### Status ladder

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `open` | Not implemented, or contradicted at HEAD. |
| `partial` | Partly implemented, or implemented with a known defect. |
| `implemented` | Present in source. Not proven by an automated test of this requirement. |
| `tested` | An automated test exercises it and passes at the tested revision (baseline: 905/905 CLI, 266/266 Rust). |
| `visually-accepted` | A human or independent PTY review accepted the rendered behaviour. |
| `product-qualified` | Passed the v1 qualification in ACCEPTANCE.md on the RC. **No requirement holds this status today.** |

Independent acceptance is recorded separately in the "Indep." column: **Y** = an independent review accepted it; **N** = self-assessed only; **—** = not applicable.

### Release classes

| Class | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **B** | BLOCKER. v1.0.0 cannot ship without it. |
| **RR** | Release-required. Must be done for v1.0.0; it is not a safety or workflow blocker on its own, but the release gate checks it. |
| **P** | Post-v1. |
| **K** | Keep: already met; protected by regression tests. |

### Evidence labels

| Label | Kind of evidence |
|---|---|
| SRC | source inspection |
| TEST | automated test |
| RT | live runtime observation (including PTY) |
| MEAS | measurement |
| DOC | documentation claim |
| HIST | historical or reported evidence |
| INF | inference |
| UNV | unknown or unverified |

- Findings are defined in [AUDIT.md](AUDIT.md).

All historical commitments are carried forward in §2. None are silently dropped. Each one is either retained, superseded or descoped, with a written disposition.

## 1. Legend

### Status ladder

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `open` | Not implemented, or contradicted at HEAD. |
| `partial` | Partly implemented, or implemented with a known defect. |
| `implemented` | Present in source. Not proven by an automated test of this requirement. |
| `tested` | An automated test exercises it and passes at the tested revision (baseline: 905/905 CLI, 266/266 Rust). |
| `visually-accepted` | A human or independent PTY review accepted the rendered behaviour. |
| `product-qualified` | Passed the v1 qualification in ACCEPTANCE.md on the RC. **No requirement holds this status today.** |

Independent acceptance is recorded separately in the "Indep." column: **Y** = an independent review accepted it; **N** = self-assessed only; **—** = not applicable.

### Release classes

| Class | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **B** | BLOCKER. v1.0.0 cannot ship without it. |
| **RR** | Release-required. Must be done for v1.0.0; it is not a safety or workflow blocker on its own, but the release gate checks it. |
| **P** | Post-v1. |
| **K** | Keep: already met; protected by regression tests. |

| Label | Kind of evidence |
|---|---|
| SRC | source inspection |
| TEST | automated test |
| RT | live runtime observation (including PTY) |
| MEAS | measurement |
| DOC | documentation claim |
| HIST | historical or reported evidence |
| INF | inference |
| UNV | unknown or unverified |

- Findings are defined in [AUDIT.md](AUDIT.md).

| | |

| Audit date | 2026-10-14 |
| Tested revision | `db1ca55` (`main`, `v0.1.0-alpha.2-2-gdb1ca55`) |
| Scope | Full first-party repository. Coverage ledger in §4. |
| Conclusion | **v1.0.0 readiness is NOT established. It is BLOCKED.** There are 33 blocker requirements across 11 workstreams, plus qualification evidence that does not yet exist. |

This document reports implementation state and audit evidence only. It is not an independent acceptance (see §8). Client release readiness and contest readiness are assessed separately (§7).

## 1. Project identity

| Repository root | `/home/mike/nexus-code` | RT |

The commit is pushed (git status clean apart from one untracked directory). | RT (`git remote -v`, `git status`) |
| Working tree | Clean except the untracked `nexus-continuity-validation/` (user's; preserved). Two stashes (`stash@{0}` continuity and instruction-precedence work; `stash@{1}` pre-sync) preserved untouched. 90 worktrees exist (not inspected). | RT |
| Versions | `package.json` and `cli/package.json`: `0.1.0-alpha.2`. **`core/Cargo.toml`: `1.2.1`** (mismatch, REL-04). Tags on origin: `v0.1.0-alpha.1` and `v0.1.0-alpha.2`, both GitHub prereleases. Local-only tags `v1.1.0`, `v1.2.0`, `v1.2.1` (never on the remote, per the owner and `git ls-remote`). | RT |
| Build entry points | `make build` (cargo release + `tsc`), `make test` (cargo test + `npm --prefix cli test` + `scripts/security_gates.sh`), `scripts/package-linux.sh`, `scripts/smoke-package.sh`, `scripts/installer-smoke.sh`. CI: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (contest contract job + `linux-x86_64`), `release.yml` (tag-triggered). A dead `.gitlab-ci.yml` also exists. | SRC |
| Toolchain at audit | node v24.21.0, npm 11.19.0, cargo/rustc 1.95.0, Ubuntu (kernel 6.8), glibc 2.39 | RT |
| Installed launchers | `~/.local/bin/nexus` → published package `v0.1.0-alpha.2` (`a2e94f3`), **first on PATH**. `/usr/local/bin/nexus` → `~/nexus-code/harness.sh` (checkout build, reports `0.1.0-alpha.2 (db1ca5580860, main)`). Plain `nexus` on this host therefore runs the published package, not the checkout. | RT |
| Runtime services | The local inference gateway is configured in `~/.config/nexus/config.env`: endpoint `https://10.0.8.5:8443/v1`, model `engineering/b0`, key redacted, `LOCAL_HARNESS_SHELL=bash`. The repo-tracked `cli/.env` holds LM Studio defaults (`localhost:1234`, key "local"). **The audit sent no requests to the gateway or to any cloud provider.** | RT (values redacted) |
| External dependencies | Node ≥ 20 (runtime), GitHub Releases (installer), optional bubblewrap/Docker (sandbox), optional cloud providers (OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, ChatGPT/Copilot OAuth, compatible), optional MCP servers, DuckDuckGo (default `search_web`). | SRC |
| Issue tracker | GitHub: 0 issues, 0 PRs. Historical Issues #10–#13 lived in a prior tracker and are referenced only in docs. | RT (`gh`) |

## 2. Product contract for v1.0.0

### 2.1 Established commitments (sources: README, quickstart, USER_MANUAL, COMPACTION_AND_CONTINUITY, CLOUD_PROVIDERS, release notes, Issue #12 and later reviews; ledger in REQUIREMENTS §2)

- **Users and workflows.** A single developer or operator runs supervised coding tasks in local repositories on Linux x86-64. The workflows are:
  - the interactive live TUI (primary);
  - the REPL;
  - headless `nexus run` with JSON output and exit codes;
  - resume (`-r`, `/resume`, `run --resume`);
  - `nexus doctor`;
  - workspace trust;
  - providers and connect;
  - checkpoints and undo;
  - MCP client and server;
  - skills and plugins;
  - `/team` and `nexus operation`.
- **Local inference is first class.** Nexus works against any OpenAI-compatible local server (LM Studio, vLLM). The homelab-ai gateway is an optional integration, and Nexus must operate without it.
- **Honest outcomes.** VERIFIED only from a real, bound verifier pass. UNVERIFIED, REGRESSION_FREE, BLOCKED and LIMIT_REACHED are distinct.
- **No default step ceiling.** Turns end on completion, cancel, stagnation or failure.
- **Safety promises.**
  - Path jail.
  - Workspace extensions only after `nexus trust`.
  - Secrets tokenized on egress.
  - Credential origin scoping.
  - Cloud destinations only by operator choice.
  - Approvals cannot be decided by stray typing.
- **Distribution.** A one-line non-root installer with SHA-256 verification, version pinning, upgrade and rollback by re-running, manual uninstall that keeps user data, and Linux x86-64 / glibc ≥ 2.35 / Node ≥ 20 only.

### 2.2 Proposed v1.0.0 maturity definition

Nexus v1.0.0 means all of the following:

1. **Safe by default on untrusted input.** Content from a repository, a web page, a skill or a tool output cannot cause unapproved host execution, egress, or configuration changes.
2. **Owns its processes.** Stop means stopped.
3. **Truthful.** No false VERIFIED. Bounded, typed failures.
4. **Continuous.** Resume and compaction never silently lose state.
5. **Standalone.** Qualified live on at least 2 non-gateway local servers.
6. **Shippable.** The installed product equals the tested product, and the documented commands work. One version identity, license notices, SBOM and provenance.
7. **Qualified.** Held-out matched evaluation, plus fault injection, meeting the pre-registered thresholds in DEC-05.

### 2.3 Classification

| Category | Location |
|---|---|
| Blockers, release-required work, post-v1 work | REQUIREMENTS.md §3, §5 |
| Decisions | DECISIONS.md. All resolved under delegated owner authority (2026-10-14). |
| Optional improvements after v1 | REQUIREMENTS §5 |

Each blocker is justified by a workflow, a safety requirement, a compatibility commitment or a reproduced failure (see its "Rationale" and "Finding" columns).

## 3. Architecture as implemented

```
 operator ─┬─► nexus (packaged: node index.js → REPL)          ◄── REL-01: no route to TUI
           └─► harness.sh (checkout) ─► nexus-tui --live (Rust, Ratatui)
                                           │ NDJSON protocol (stdin/stdout)
                                           ▼
                                 node sidecar.js  ──or──  node index.js repl/run
                                           │ (in-process)
                                           ▼
            ApplicationCore / AutonomousAgent.runTurn  (cli/src/agent.ts, 5.4k lines)
              steering drain → capability refresh → admission (compaction ladder, findings,
              token count) → ProviderRecoveryController → streaming inference (client.ts)
              → parse (parser.ts) → dispatch (approval gate) → ExecutionSpine/authority
              → RustCoreBridge (tools.ts) ── JSON-RPC stdio ──► harness-core rpc (Rust)
              → observe/ExecutionTracker → endStep → durable state (~/.nexus/tasks, sessions)
                                                                 │
     inference: OpenAI-compatible (local/gateway) | Responses | Anthropic | OAuth providers
     verifier: tester.ts discoverVerifier → harness-core run_command (repo test script)
     extensions: MCP (stdio/remote), plugins (in-process import), skills (prompt injection)
```

### 3.1 Trust boundaries and their state at HEAD

| Boundary | Intended control | Actual state (finding) |
|---|---|---|
| Model → host shell | Approval or sandbox | Default auto with no sandbox (SEC-01); verifier runs bypass even review mode (VER-01); prose and reasoning JSON executed (VER-02/03) |
| Model → network | Egress classification, approval | Ungated in review mode (HIST-05); SSRF guard is string-based (SEC-03) |
| Workspace → configuration | Only allowlisted project settings | `.env` overrides any env, including TLS (PRV-01) |
| Workspace → prompt | Trust-gated | MCP and plugins are gated; skills and knowledge are not (SEC-05, AGT-10) |
| Destination locality | IP-based | Prefix strings (PRV-02, PRV-08) |
| Operator cancel → processes | Kill the tree | Not propagated; orphans on exit (TUI-01, SEC-07) |
| File tools → filesystem | Jail | **Sound** (C §4 R1) |
| Credentials → destinations | Origin-bound | **Sound** (B §5), except the TLS downgrade path |
| Durable state → other users | 0600/0700 | Mostly 664/775 (PER-01) |

### 3.2 Data flow for persistence and recovery

- **Task state.** `~/.nexus/tasks/<id>.json`, written as a full atomic rewrite on each progress event. The compaction archive is `<id>.history.jsonl` (append + fsync).
- **Sessions.** `~/.nexus/sessions`.
- **Other stores.** Checkpoints at `~/.nexus/checkpoints` plus `refs/nexus/checkpoints/*`. The audit log at `~/.nexus/audit.log`. Flights at `<ws>/.nexus/flights`.
- **Recovery.** `recoverFromTaskState` restores messages and objective, and filters uncommitted archive entries. **Except:** `run --resume` discards the restored conversation (AGT-01), and work units skip the commit protocol (AGT-02).

## 4. Coverage ledger and methods

Methods:

- Seven parallel scoped audits plus one gap-fill audit. Each produced a per-file coverage table (`evidence/*_*.md` §1).
- A clean-snapshot baseline build and test, plus a git-clone baseline run in CI order.

## 8. Strengths supported by evidence

- **Test discipline.**
  - 905/905 CLI tests (including PTY TUI end-to-end suites), 266/266 Rust tests and the security gates pass in a clean clone run in CI order. Evidence: `evidence/baseline/baseline2.log`.
  - CI runs the same suite before every release.
- **Outcome-honesty architecture.**
  - A single result derivation with invariants.
  - Fail-before/pass-after independence for discovered verifiers.
  - Truncated replies are never executed.
  - Positive completion evidence is required before tool calls run.
  - Evidence: A §5, B §5.
- **No artificial step ceiling.** Evidence-based stagnation detection. Bounded provider recovery with a well-typed failure taxonomy. Evidence: A §5, B §5.
- **Live TUI approval input safety** held under every adversarial PTY test: typing across the panel, paste, bursts and resize. Evidence: D §5.
- **Sound file-tool path jail.** Credential origin scoping. Trust gating for MCP and plugins. Evidence: C §5, B §5.
- **Release engineering.**
  - The release is gated on main.
  - Same-runner byte-reproducible packages.
  - Installer and package smoke tests.
  - A safe non-root installer with working upgrade and rollback.
  - A well-built `doctor` with narrow, confirmed, idempotent repairs.
  - Evidence: E §5.
- **Self-critical history.** The project's own reviews repeatedly refused to over-claim: Issue #12 left open, the eval pilot self-graded NOT QUALIFIED. Evidence: F §5.

## 9. Limitations of this audit

- No live inference was run against any model server. All inference behaviour is from mocks, fixtures and historical records.
- No cloud calls.
- No Cloudflare deployment.
- No real-terminal emulators: pyte emulation only.
- No macOS or other distributions.
- No cross-runner reproducibility check.
- Unreviewed regions are listed in §4.
- Severity ratings are the reviewers' judgement. Several INF items (AGT-09, PRV-06 server behaviour, VER-08, VER-09 ratios) need the qualification procedures in the evidence files.
- The baseline test runs wrote task records into the operator's real `~/.nexus/tasks` (PER-03). See EVIDENCE §5.

## 2. Product contract for v1.0.0

### 2.1 Established commitments (sources: README, quickstart, USER_MANUAL, COMPACTION_AND_CONTINUITY, CLOUD_PROVIDERS, release notes, Issue #12 and later reviews; ledger in REQUIREMENTS §2)

- **Users and workflows.** A single developer or operator runs supervised coding tasks in local repositories on Linux x86-64. The workflows are:
  - the interactive live TUI (primary);
  - the REPL;
  - headless `nexus run` with JSON output and exit codes;
  - resume (`-r`, `/resume`, `run --resume`);
  - `nexus doctor`;
  - workspace trust;
  - providers and connect;
  - checkpoints and undo;
  - MCP client and server;
  - skills and plugins;
  - `/team` and `nexus operation`.
- **Local inference is first class.** Nexus works against any OpenAI-compatible local server (LM Studio, vLLM). The homelab-ai gateway is an optional integration, and Nexus must operate without it.
- **Honest outcomes.** VERIFIED only from a real, bound verifier pass. UNVERIFIED, REGRESSION_FREE, BLOCKED and LIMIT_REACHED are distinct.
- **No default step ceiling.** Turns end on completion, cancel, stagnation or failure.
- **Safety promises.**
  - Path jail.
  - Workspace extensions only after `nexus trust`.
  - Secrets tokenized on egress.
  - Credential origin scoping.
  - Cloud destinations only by operator choice.
  - Approvals cannot be decided by stray typing.
- **Distribution.** A one-line non-root installer with SHA-256 verification, version pinning, upgrade and rollback by re-running, manual uninstall that keeps user data, and Linux x86-64 / glibc ≥ 2.35 / Node ≥ 20 only.

### 2.2 Proposed v1.0.0 maturity definition

Nexus v1.0.0 means all of the following:

1. **Safe by default on untrusted input.** Content from a repository, a web page, a skill or a tool output cannot cause unapproved host execution, egress, or configuration changes.
2. **Owns its processes.** Stop means stopped.
3. **Truthful.** No false VERIFIED. Bounded, typed failures.
4. **Continuous.** Resume and compaction never silently lose state.
5. **Standalone.** Qualified live on at least 2 non-gateway local servers.
6. **Shippable.** The installed product equals the tested product, and the documented commands work. One version identity, license notices, SBOM and provenance.
7. **Qualified.** Held-out matched evaluation, plus fault injection, meeting the pre-registered thresholds in DEC-05.

### 2.3 Classification

| Category | Location |
|---|---|
| Blockers, release-required work, post-v1 work | REQUIREMENTS.md §3, §5 |
| Decisions | DECISIONS.md. All resolved under delegated owner authority (2026-10-14). |
| Optional improvements after v1 | REQUIREMENTS §5 |

Each blocker is justified by a workflow, a safety requirement, a compatibility commitment or a reproduced failure (see its "Rationale" and "Finding" columns).

## 3. Architecture as implemented

```
 operator ─┬─► nexus (packaged: node index.js → REPL)          ◄── REL-01: no route to TUI
           └─► harness.sh (checkout) ─► nexus-tui --live (Rust, Ratatui)
                                           │ NDJSON protocol (stdin/stdout)
                                           ▼
                                 node sidecar.js  ──or──  node index.js repl/run
                                           │ (in-process)
                                           ▼
            ApplicationCore / AutonomousAgent.runTurn  (cli/src/agent.ts, 5.4k lines)
              steering drain → capability refresh → admission (compaction ladder, findings,
              token count) → ProviderRecoveryController → streaming inference (client.ts)
              → parse (parser.ts) → dispatch (approval gate) → ExecutionSpine/authority
              → RustCoreBridge (tools.ts) ── JSON-RPC stdio ──► harness-core rpc (Rust)
              → observe/ExecutionTracker → endStep → durable state (~/.nexus/tasks, sessions)
                                                                 │
     inference: OpenAI-compatible (local/gateway) | Responses | Anthropic | OAuth providers
     verifier: tester.ts discoverVerifier → harness-core run_command (repo test script)
     extensions: MCP (stdio/remote), plugins (in-process import), skills (prompt injection)
```

### 3.1 Trust boundaries and their state at HEAD

| Boundary | Intended control | Actual state (finding) |
|---|---|---|
| Model → host shell | Approval or sandbox | Default auto with no sandbox (SEC-01); verifier runs bypass even review mode (VER-01); prose and reasoning JSON executed (VER-02/03) |
| Model → network | Egress classification, approval | Ungated in review mode (HIST-05); SSRF guard is string-based (SEC-03) |
| Workspace → configuration | Only allowlisted project settings | `.env` overrides any env, including TLS (PRV-01) |
| Workspace → prompt | Trust-gated | MCP and plugins are gated; skills and knowledge are not (SEC-05, AGT-10) |
| Destination locality | IP-based | Prefix strings (PRV-02, PRV-08) |
| Operator cancel → processes | Kill the tree | Not propagated; orphans on exit (TUI-01, SEC-07) |
| File tools → filesystem | Jail | **Sound** (C §4 R1) |
| Credentials → destinations | Origin-bound | **Sound** (B §5), except the TLS downgrade path |
| Durable state → other users | 0600/0700 | Mostly 664/775 (PER-01) |

### 3.2 Data flow for persistence and recovery

- **Task state.** `~/.nexus/tasks/<id>.json`, written as a full atomic rewrite on each progress event. The compaction archive is `<id>.history.jsonl` (append + fsync).
- **Sessions.** `~/.nexus/sessions`.
- **Other stores.** Checkpoints at `~/.nexus/checkpoints` plus `refs/nexus/checkpoints/*`. The audit log at `~/.nexus/audit.log`. Flights at `<ws>/.nexus/flights`.
- **Recovery.** `recoverFromTaskState` restores messages and objective, and filters uncommitted archive entries. **Except:** `run --resume` discards the restored conversation (AGT-01), and work units skip the commit protocol (AGT-02).

## 2. Product contract for v1.0.0

### 2.1 Established commitments (sources: README, quickstart, USER_MANUAL, COMPACTION_AND_CONTINUITY, CLOUD_PROVIDERS, release notes, Issue #12 and later reviews; ledger in REQUIREMENTS §2)

- **Users and workflows.** A single developer or operator runs supervised coding tasks in local repositories on Linux x86-64. The workflows are:
  - the interactive live TUI (primary);
  - the REPL;
  - headless `nexus run` with JSON output and exit codes;
  - resume (`-r`, `/resume`, `run --resume`);
  - `nexus doctor`;
  - workspace trust;
  - providers and connect;
  - checkpoints and undo;
  - MCP client and server;
  - skills and plugins;
  - `/team` and `nexus operation`.
- **Local inference is first class.** Nexus works against any OpenAI-compatible local server (LM Studio, vLLM). The homelab-ai gateway is an optional integration, and Nexus must operate without it.
- **Honest outcomes.** VERIFIED only from a real, bound verifier pass. UNVERIFIED, REGRESSION_FREE, BLOCKED and LIMIT_REACHED are distinct.
- **No default step ceiling.** Turns end on completion, cancel, stagnation or failure.
- **Safety promises.**

  - Secrets tokenized on egress.
  - Credential origin scoping.

### 2.2 Proposed v1.0.0 maturity definition

Nexus v1.0.0 means all of the following:

1. **Safe by default on untrusted input.** Content from a repository, a web page, a skill or a tool output cannot cause unapproved host execution, egress, or configuration changes.
2. **Owns its processes.** Stop means stopped.
3. **Truthful.** No false VERIFIED. Bounded, typed failures.
4. **Continuous.** Resume and compaction never silently lose state.
5. **Standalone.** Qualified live on at least 2 non-gateway local servers.
6. **Shippable.** The installed product equals the tested product, and the documented commands work. One version identity, license notices, SBOM and provenance.
7. **Qualified.** Held-out matched evaluation, plus fault injection, meeting the pre-registered thresholds in DEC-05.
